chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from one of the two عليهما السلام, concerning:

A man gouged out another man’s eye, cut off his nose and his ears, and then killed him. He عليه السلام said: “If he did that separately, then qiṣāṣ is carried out against him for that, and then he is killed. But if he struck him with one single blow, his neck is struck, and qiṣāṣ is not carried out against him.”

key_terms.أَنْفَهُ: his nose, one of the organs mentioned in the injury
key_terms.أُذُنَيْهِ: his two ears, indicating multiple bodily injuries
key_terms.اقْتُصَّ: qiṣāṣ was carried out, meaning retaliatory legal retribution
key_terms.ضُرِبَ عُنُقُهُ: his neck is struck, meaning he is executed
key_terms.فَقَأَ: gouged out or ruptured, referring here to destroying the eye
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: he is killed, referring to capital retaliation

ai.seo_question: If someone mutilates a person and then kills him, is qiṣāṣ carried out for the injuries as well as the killing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding qiṣāṣ when a victim suffers multiple bodily injuries before being killed. It distinguishes between injuries inflicted separately, which entail qiṣāṣ before execution, and a single fatal blow, in which only execution is carried out.
